description: G-Set CRDT cross-language conformance (the bottom rung of the algebra ladder; B-0954 bus comms substrate). Every impl starts from `initialSet`, replays `ops` in order with the canonical string comparator, and must value-match `expectedReplayStates[i]` after op i AND `expectedFinalState` at the end. Sets are serialized in canonical ascending order, so equality is array-equality. Oracle #1 = TS reference; F# casts oracle #2; C#/Rust join later per the meet-in-the-middle 4-oracle.
comparator: ascending ordinal / UTF-16 code-unit order (TS `<` / C# StringComparer.Ordinal / byte-ordered Rust `Ord`). NOTE: the F# G-Set oracle currently sorts via `Comparer<'T>.Default` (src/Core/GSet.fs), which for string is culture-sensitive (not ordinal); it coincides with ordinal for these ASCII keys — where ordinal also equals Unicode code-point order — so all four oracles agree on these vectors, but moving F# to ordinal for true non-ASCII parity is a known gap. Astral-plane keys (UTF-16 code-unit vs code-point divergence) are out of scope for the v1 contract.

ops.note: commutative+associative: unsorted input, b-001 already present
identity: union with empty is a no-op

laws.associative: union(union(a, b), c) == union(a, union(b, c))
